# v0.30.4: a user message kept in the prompt and in the store after compaction

v0.30.4 is a patch release on v0.30.2. Its main fix: a compaction pass could drop a user message from the prompt, and a message the host carried only in a hidden `api_content` field was never stored ([#3087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3087)). This release stores that message and hands the host back its own user rows after a pass that makes no progress.

v0.30.4 also carries the v0.30.3 hotfix for the summary head stored again after a same-length pass ([#3041](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3041)), with the v0.30.3-rc2 rule that keeps a repeated user message in the prompt ([#3061](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3061)), rebuilt for this line. The recall tools now skip a proven copy of the summary head, and `/lcm status` and the doctor warn about two problems that were silent before. It adds one setting, off by default, and no schema change. The [v0.30.2 notes](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/tag/v0.30.2) and the [v0.30.3 notes](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/tag/v0.30.3) still apply, except where this page says otherwise.

## Changes since v0.30.2

- **A message the host carried only in a hidden `api_content` field is now stored** ([#3087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3087), by [#3089](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3089)). Hermes can put a user message only inside another user row's `api_content`, as a complete out-of-band message block, while that row's own text is a different message. Earlier versions stored the row's text and nothing else, so once the host rewrote or compacted the row, the hidden message was gone from the store and from recall. v0.30.4 finds such a block and stores it once as a recall-only row beside the session. A block that carries the host's gateway id is stored once across a row move, a restart, a compaction rewrite and a session rotation; an edited message counts as a new message. Two routes can still store a block without a gateway id a second time; neither loses anything, and the copies never enter the prompt: a same-conversation session rotation that replays the carrier row, and a fast session end after an in-place compaction drops an earlier identical user row ([#3102](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3102)). A busy retry at session end is a third ([#3092](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3092)). The hook context that the host adds to `api_content` on every turn is not stored. The recall-only row never enters the prompt, proactive recall or cleanup; `lcm_grep`, `lcm_recall` and `lcm_expand` find it. If storing it fails, host ingest still succeeds (unless SQLite aborts the whole transaction, for example on a full disk), and `/lcm status` shows a failure count and time.
- **After a compaction pass that makes no progress, LCM-X hands the host back its own user rows unchanged** ([#3087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3087), by [#3094](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3094)). This is the second half of the fix. On v0.30.2 and v0.30.3, such a pass could return LCM-X's own cached copy of a user row, emptied or shortened, and the host then saved that list. A user message could leave the prompt this way; it stayed in the store, so recall still found it. v0.30.4 returns each of the host's user rows unchanged, content and `api_content` included, at its base position. With the change above, both halves of the fix for the issue are in this release; the forms of hidden message it does not recover yet are listed under Known issues.
- **A same-length compaction pass no longer makes the next ingest store the summary head again** ([#3041](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3041)). This is the v0.30.3 hotfix, carried on this line. A copy already stored stays stored, out of the prompt and out of compaction. The [v0.30.3 notes](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/tag/v0.30.3) describe it in full.
- **A new user message that repeats an earlier one word for word stays in the prompt and in recall** ([#3061](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3061), by [#3086](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3086)). This is the v0.30.3-rc2 rule, rebuilt on this line's head-copy check: a stored row that holds a summary head and then a user message counts as LCM-X's own copy only when that message binds to its own earlier occurrence. When the evidence is missing or ambiguous, the row stays visible. The worst case is a duplicate summary head, with one exception in Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, described under Known issues ([#3103](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3103)).
- **The recall tools skip a proven copy of the summary head** ([#3047](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3047)). `lcm_grep`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_load_session`, `lcm_recall` and the recall readers now leave out a stored row proven to be LCM-X's own summary head, using the same check as the prompt and compaction. This was a v0.30.3 known issue. Stored rows are unchanged.
- **The head-copy check costs less** ([#3062](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3062), by [#3086](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3086)). The publication write no longer checks rows it then throws away. In the change's timing cell (100,000 rows, and 100 stored rows that each hold a summary head and then a user message), a compaction pass went from 15.1 s to 12.2 s. Some cost remains (see Known issues).
- **The stub-only exit keeps the host's rows and replaces only the stubbed tool outputs** ([#3067](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3067)). Before, a compaction pass that only replaces older tool outputs with short stubs rebuilt the whole list. It could fold the unchanged summary head into the next user row, which rewrote the provider's cached prompt from the start and, after a restart, stored that folded row again. Now the exit returns the host's own list with only the stubbed tool rows changed. A head the host merged with the next user row is still rebuilt, and the exit falls back to the old behaviour when any check fails.
- **After the host refuses a compaction pass, the next pass drops a replayed row only when every row it absorbed is covered by a summary** ([#3052](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3052)). Merged rows that were only partly covered could otherwise be left behind, and compaction could stop until the survival cut ([#3006](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3006)). A reply that no summary covers is never dropped. A failed write of the "refused" mark is retried.
- **`/lcm status` and the doctor warn when the linked SQLite has the WAL-reset bug** ([#3058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3058), by [#3085](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3085)). With SQLite older than 3.51.3 (apart from the patched 3.50.7+ and 3.44.6+ builds), `/lcm status` shows a `sqlite_wal_reset: warn` line, `/lcm doctor` and the `lcm_doctor` tool show a warning with the upgrade as the recommended action, and the startup log line says what the bug can do. It is a warning, never a failure. An unaffected version leaves every output as before.
- **`/lcm status` and the doctor show compaction passes that free nothing** ([#3081](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3081), by [#3084](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3084)). `/lcm status` shows `hidden_only_streak`, and the doctor warns after three passes in a row that free no host rows. This makes the stall visible; it does not fix it (see Known issues).

## Optional features

- **Turn-start defer gate, `LCM_TURN_START_DEFER_CEILING` (environment variable only), off by default** ([#3084](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3084)). While the context is under the ceiling, an automatic compaction pass in the middle of a tool turn waits for the next turn start. The value is a share of the model window: `0`, the default, turns it off, and any other value must be above 0 and below 1 minus the survival reserve (`LCM_SURVIVAL_RESERVE`, default 0.15). An invalid value is ignored with a config warning. When it is on, LCM-X warns if the ceiling is inert or not tied to the trigger, logs one line per deferral episode, and shows its counters in `/lcm status`. Its rehearsal ran on another build, not on this one: before you turn it on for a live profile, rehearse it on the v0.30.4 build first.

## Known issues

- **Limits of the hidden-message recovery: some forms are still not recovered.** v0.30.4 recovers a message from `api_content` only when it is a complete out-of-band message block. A message carried in any other form is not stored. Four smaller limits of the same change:
  - After a session rotation, `lcm_grep` at its default scope in the new session does not find a recovered message from the old session; `session_scope: all` does.
  - A block quoted by a host hook can still be stored as a recovered message when the row's own text is itself a complete block, or when the row is not plain text (for example a message with an image) or its text is not at the start of `api_content`. LCM-X stores it rather than risk losing a real message. A hook-aware boundary is planned for v0.30.5 ([#3091](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3091)).
  - A retry after a busy database at session end can store a recovered block twice when the block has no gateway id. Nothing is lost. A fix is planned for v0.31.0 ([#3092](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3092)).
  - Recall can show a message twice. Nothing is lost, and a fix is planned for v0.30.5 ([#3102](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3102)). A block without a gateway id can be stored a second time after a same-conversation rotation that replays its carrier row (one copy per new session), or at a fast session end after an in-place compaction drops an earlier identical user row (at most one extra copy). The copies never enter the prompt.
- **Compaction passes can free no host rows while the walk crosses stored rows the host no longer shows** ([#3081](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3081)). What a user sees: on a long-running store, compaction can run for two to three minutes on about a dozen turns in a row, and the context does not shrink. v0.30.4 shows the stall in `/lcm status` (`hidden_only_streak`) and the doctor. There is no workaround. The fix is now planned for v0.30.5, a patch release after v0.30.4.
- **After a refused compaction pass, a restart or a merged tool row can still leave compaction stuck** ([#3006](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3006), compaction stuck after the host refuses a pass; [#3053](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3053), a held fix for the "refused" mark not honoured after a cold restart). After the host refuses a compaction pass that stored summaries, a restart before the refusal is recorded can still leave compaction stuck until the survival cut, and a merged row whose tool-calling row has no text still blocks the next pass. Nothing is lost from the store; rows the survival cut removes stay stored and can be recalled. Fix release not yet set.
- **Durable sensitive-pattern redaction (`LCM_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS_ENABLED`) is unsupported: not maintained; do not enable** ([#3096](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3096), docs in [#3097](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3097)). It stays off by default, and a bug that occurs only with it enabled will not be fixed. If you already enabled it, set it to `false`: rows it already redacted stay redacted, and new content is then stored without redaction. The cloud embedding privacy filter is a separate setting and is not affected.
- **With sensitive patterns off, a user row that quotes LCM-X's redaction-marker text can lose a late host annotation on a cache-hit compaction pass** ([#3099](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3099)). When a user row's text quotes LCM-X's literal redaction-marker text, a compaction pass served from LCM-X's cache hands back LCM-X's shorter cached copy of that row, so the host gets the row back without a host annotation added late and without its `api_content`. v0.30.2 behaves the same, and nothing is lost from the store.
- **A store on SQLite older than 3.51.3 can lose whole recent transactions.** With SQLite before 3.51.3, a store in WAL mode with several connections can lose whole recent transactions, through SQLite's own WAL-reset bug ([#1085](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1085); evidence in [#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)). This is a storage-layer loss below LCM-X. v0.30.4 now warns about it in `/lcm status` and the doctor, but cannot prevent it: upgrade SQLite. Check your SQLite with `python3 -c "import sqlite3; print(sqlite3.sqlite_version)"`.
- **The head-copy check can still cost a lookup on every turn for a carrier whose message matches an earlier one** ([#3062](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3062)). v0.30.4 reduces this cost but does not remove it: each such row still costs a lookup on every turn while it stays in the prompt window, and a cache for that lookup is planned.
- **The transcript repair for replies lost before v0.30.2 is not in this release** ([#3022](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3022)). Hermes's own transcript still holds those replies. The release for this repair is not yet set.
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=off`, the summary head can still be stored again** ([#3060](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3060)). If the host's save stamps the emitted head with a timestamp, a row id and a new uid, the next ingest stores the head again exactly as v0.30.2 does. Nothing is lost. With the setting unset (the default) or `on`, the fix holds. It is not in this release. A fix is planned for v0.31.0.
- **After a restart, a tool call and its stubbed result can be stored a second time when a compaction pass had only stubbed tool outputs** ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674), [#3026](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3026)). Sometimes a pass only replaces older tool outputs with short stubs. If the engine then restarts, the next ingest does not match those stubs to the stored originals, and it stores each call and stub again. Nothing is lost. A context rebuilt from the store can then carry each of those tool calls twice. On the host's compress path no measured case sent a tool call twice in a model request; the duplicates appear only when a context is rebuilt from the store itself. v0.30.4 no longer stores the folded summary head in this case ([#3067](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3067)), but it still stores the tool pairs again. v0.30.2 behaves the same for the tool pairs ([#3073](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3073)). Matching a stub to its stored original after a restart is planned as its own fix.
- **Two kinds of stored head copy still reach the prompt, as on v0.30.2.** Each shows up as a duplicate summary head; no message is lost.
  - A carrier stored before v0.30.0, whose message has no matching host timestamp. Those versions recorded no emission for it, so this release cannot prove it is a copy and keeps it.
  - A copy stored in a child session after a session rotation, when the message it carries has no matching host timestamp and its earlier occurrence is in the parent session. A child-session copy is now recognised and left out when it holds only the summary head, or when its message matches an earlier message with the same host timestamp.
- **With Hermes's legacy rotating compaction (`compression.in_place: false`, now or earlier; the default in-place mode creates no compaction child), a carried message can be missing from the new session's default-scope recall** ([#3103](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3103)). It needs a rotation that the parent session's end did not adopt. The new session's copy of the message is then treated as a known copy: `lcm_grep` at its default scope and `lcm_expand` in that session do not return it. The prompt is unchanged, and nothing is deleted: `session_scope: all` finds the message in the old session. A fix is planned for v0.30.5.
- **In the default uid mode and with `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, a user message that is an exact paste of the current summary head, with nothing after it, is treated as a copy** ([#3047](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3047)). The row stays stored, but it is left out of the prompt, compaction and recall. This is an accepted tradeoff, pinned by a test. A paste of the summary head followed by another message stays visible ([#3086](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3086)).
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, a stub-first exit can return a summary together with the raw rows it covers** ([#3048](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3048)). This is v0.30.2 behaviour. A fix has to keep the rule that only a committing pass changes the rows it returns, so it is planned for v0.31.0, after a design review.
- **Under overflow, one fitted request can leave out rows that no summary covers yet** ([#3064](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3064)). When a request is over the model's window, the survival fit trims it to fit. That one request can omit rows not yet covered by a summary, including a recent user message. The next compaction pass covers them, and nothing is lost from the store. This is v0.30.2 behaviour. A fix is planned for v0.31.0.
- **With `max_assembly_tokens` set below the host's own overhead, a forced-overflow pass can return an empty list** ([#3072](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3072)). It cannot happen at the default settings, which set no such cap, and nothing is deleted from the store. v0.30.2 behaves the same.
- **A crash after a compaction rotation, over ACP on upstream Hermes, can store one user turn twice** ([#2507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2507)). Fix release not yet set.
- **After a crash during an upgrade from v0.27.0, a composite row is kept beside its replayed parts** ([#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506)). Fix release not yet set.
- **A tool call and its result can still be stored twice on the first ingest after a restart** ([#3026](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3026)). Nothing is lost; recall can return them twice. LCM-X keeps the copy rather than risk dropping a row.
- **When the host changes a tool result, ingest can store the calling row and an unchanged sibling row a second time, with no restart** ([#2781](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2781)). Nothing is lost; recall can return those rows twice. It was seen with `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on` on a running engine. v0.30.2 behaves the same.
- **On a large store, the first turn after a restart can wait about 75 seconds, and recall can show re-stored copies** ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674), [#3111](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3111)). After a restart, the first compaction pass holds the store while it works. On a large test store (704,695 stored messages, with 1,784 rows in the restarted session's list) that took about 74 seconds, and the first turn waited about 75 seconds before reaching the model; later turns took under a second. A turn that arrives during that hold can wait a little over 30 seconds twice, at a pre-turn check and at its store write (about a minute in all in tests), and then skip the store write. In tests the skipped message was stored at the next restart in both settings, and by the next turn with `on`; nothing was lost. The same first pass stored 580 to 1,625 rows a second time (the restart copies of #1674), so recall can show those messages twice. Nothing is lost. On a store built from the same inputs, v0.30.3 shows the same counts, including the stalls below; one cell after a killed compaction pass differed once (see Qualification). With the opt-in `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, the test cell's compaction stopped shrinking at 1,470 rows; at the default setting with a 60-second compaction budget, it stopped at 568 rows. The cause of both is not yet known, and `on` is not the default.
- **Older issues that stay open.**
  - A slow first ingest after a host change, with compaction stuck behind it ([#2818](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2818)). Re-timed on v0.30.2: in the test cell the slow first ingest still takes 38 to 40 seconds, over the 30-second bar.
  - Compaction that stops on the same row at every pass ([#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162)), reported on a v0.30.1 release candidate. There is no workaround yet.
  - A store already stuck behind an old hidden-only leaf stays stuck ([#1141](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1141)), seen on v0.28.1. There is no known way to reach this state at the default settings. There is no in-place repair and no workaround yet.
  - Restart copies ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)): at a cold restart, tool results and replies that the host sends without a timestamp can be stored again, one more copy per restart. Nothing is lost. v0.30.4 does not change this, and the fix release is not yet set.

## Upgrade and rollback

- **Upgrade.** No schema change: no new tables, columns or migrations, and the schema version is unchanged. One new kind of data is written into existing tables: a recall-only copy of a message recovered from `api_content`, stored as an ordinary message in a companion session of the same conversation. Recall hits on these rows carry `session_id` `lcm-sidecar:<session id>` and `from_current_session: false`. The rows carry no sender. One new setting, `LCM_TURN_START_DEFER_CEILING`, off by default; leave it off unless you have rehearsed it on this build.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`). Then install v0.30.3 in place of this build. The store needs no conversion, because this release changes no schema. v0.30.3 has no special handling for the recall-only rows this build stored. It keeps them as ordinary stored user messages in a separate companion session of the same conversation, whose id starts with `lcm-sidecar:`. v0.30.3's clean apply can delete these rows when an ignore or stateless pattern you set matches the companion id (`lcm-sidecar:...`); take the backup first. At the default settings they do not enter the prompt. `lcm_recall`, and `lcm_grep` with `session_scope: all`, can still find them; `lcm_grep` at its default scope does not. If you turned on proactive recall or pre-answer evidence (both off by default), v0.30.3 can bring these rows into the prompt as recall from another session. While you run v0.30.3, a message the host carries only in `api_content` is not stored again, and that version's known issues apply again, including the dropped user message ([#3087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3087)).

## Qualification

This release changes ingest, compaction and recall on the turn path. The GA tag is the v0.30.4-rc1 tree plus these notes: `git diff v0.30.4-rc1 v0.30.4 --name-only` lists this file alone. So every rc1 result below is for the code this tag ships.
- CI on the tag commit: every required check passes. The tag is cut only after a pre-tag check confirms this on that exact commit. The install and startup smoke is CI's real-host job (five host builds) and its installer jobs. These are not required checks and do not run on a push to the release branch. They passed on the pull request that merged as v0.30.4-rc1, whose tree is identical to the rc1 tag commit, and they must pass on this release's notes pull request before it merges.
- The R-STABLE no-regression check (rows already handed to the host change only at a compaction commit) runs in that CI and passes.
- The test-impact intersection over this line's diff from the current user release: every mapped suite runs (45 run, 0 skipped). Three families are decided by hand: other instruments, replay and stress harnesses, and historical recorded rows.
- The smoke stage (L1) ran on this release's code and passed:
  - Reliability matrix (C1a on the seven supported host builds; C1b crash and upgrade cells): the pinned scorer could not read the summary markers from the file this release moved them to, so it reported false failures (29 rows in C1a; 15 runs across 7 of the 12 cells in C1b). Re-scored with a reader that also reads the new file, each of them passes and v0.30.3's verdicts are unchanged. In each of those 15 C1b runs, the messages LCM-X stored (every role, and the order of user messages in each session) match v0.30.3's. Reading these rows through the corrected reader departs from the bars' wording. Release decisions T1-619 and T1-621 record that departure, and the owner approved it. The original failing receipts are kept beside the re-score, and the corrected reader is now in the instrument on main, with its own test ([#3105](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3105), fixed by [#3106](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3106)). The known [#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506) cell fails on v0.30.3 too, and three ACP upgrade cells are unsupported on both builds.
  - Phase A, both postures: passes. Upgrade and rollback roundtrip with v0.30.3: passes. Fast recall tier (D1 OFF, 500 questions): 0 changed recall results against v0.30.3 (per question, for both lcm_recall and full-text search). D4 mini row: 0 net losses. D7 mini row (one seed): passes every judged bar.
  - The release review's sweep (32 finder outputs, 27 candidates voted by two model families) found no verified P0 or P1. Two duplicate shapes are a recorded v0.30.4-only exception (release decision T1-620, [#3102](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3102)); the hands-on fault cells pass on all seven host builds.
  - D1 LOCAL mini row skipped (release decision T1-622, approved by the owner), under the release standard's rule that a suite whose inputs did not change does not run: a reach check found no change in this release on the D1 harness's path that can alter the hits it returns, and the embedding modules are unchanged. This release does add per-hit checks on that path, which can lengthen recall time, so recall timing with embeddings on, and with it D1's no-timeout health condition, was not measured.
  - Both smoke checks ran on this release's exact code from a pinned main revision (27110d7a): the session switch while a compaction pass waits for its summary ([#2851](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2851)): PASS. The ordinal planner in a packed 20,000-label session ([#2840](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2840)): PASS, with 33,154 windows and 543 statements against the frozen bounds of 49,731 and 827. Both run again on the GA commit after the notes merge, and the tag is cut only if both pass.
- Live-session rows D9-D12 on a large synthetic store (counts only; one restart, then compaction passes; judged arm `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`): not all green, shipped under release decisions T1-629 and T1-631 (approved by the owner): this release matches v0.30.3 on every measure but one single-sample difference (below), on stores built from the same inputs on the same bench, and nothing is lost. v0.30.3 ran the same rows on the same bench, and both builds behave the same on them: the same compaction sequences, the same re-stored copies of [#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674) (1,625 rows at the default setting, 580 with `on`), the same stalls (at 1,470 rows with `on`, and at 568 rows at the default setting with a 60-second compaction budget), two turn waits over 30 seconds in each D10 cell, and a first turn after a restart of about 75 seconds. No stored message was lost or changed on either build. One cell differed once: after a killed compaction pass, this release's first pass ran 118 seconds, near the 120-second summary deadline, published nothing and armed a hold, and the next pass made the same reduction v0.30.3 made at once; both ended with the same rows and nothing lost. It is a single-sample difference whose cause is not known ([#3114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3114)). On this release, a turn whose store write was skipped during the cold-start hold was stored at the next restart in both settings, and also by the next turn with `on` (at the default setting, the next-turn order produced no skip in three tries); no message was missing. D12 passed in all six cells on both builds; on this release's run that reading is unqualified, because the producer's own qualification failed there on an instrument check (unexpected lock answers on the v0.30.0 baseline). Two checks of the comparison were read as the owner decided: the stores hold identical messages once the build's own time stamps are masked, and timing is compared on total held time, because a hold can split around a 30-second lock wait on either build ([#3113](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3113)).
- The Phase C live soak (30 or more turns over the host's own transport, with recall probes, at least one compaction and the doctor at the end) on seven host builds, with v0.30.3 run beside it on the same host: met (release decision T1-630, approved by the owner). In every cell of both builds: 45 turns, at least one compaction committed (9 to 15 per cell here, 3 to 17 on v0.30.3), every stored message kept with none duplicated, no level-3 summary truncated, no publication-invariant conflict, and every recall probe answered with nothing lost; exact answers were at or above v0.30.3's in every cell. The doctor and caught-trace bars are not green; they are judged by class. The doctor found 0 failed checks. Its warnings are classes v0.30.3 also shows, plus two that come from this release or the test setup: the new SQLite warning above, on the host build that links SQLite 3.45.1, and a payload warning from running the doctor on a copy of the store without its payload folder (the real store holds all four payload files). The caught tracebacks are LCM-X's known refusal when the host's background review tries to detach it (the same frames on both builds: 49 here, 64 on v0.30.3) and, on one host build, one from the host's own code tool (below); the host's optional-import failures, seen on both builds, are warning lines, not tracebacks. On one host build, the host's own code tool could not open its socket because the test kit set a very long temporary folder; that error is recorded as a test-environment fault, not an LCM-X error, and the v0.31.0 test kit is to give the host a short one.
- D7 (pacing and facts kept on the fleet's summary route), a full three-seed cell on this release's code before the tag (owner decision, release decision T1-628; all six bars judged, facts kept against the floor of 0.80): passes every bar. 14.5 compactions per 100 turns after the threshold crossing (limit 25), a mean wait of 5.2 seconds per turn (limit 15), 14.5% of turns waiting (limit 25%), facts kept 0.93 at checkpoint 304 (floor 0.80), no row dropped by a survival fit, and a 90th-percentile compaction time of 45.8 seconds (limit 120). Just before the cell started, a check found no other bench row, live-soak run, Hermes ACP or Codex process on the bench host, and both load samples taken during the cell were low.
- Run after GA, as recorded evidence (owner decision, release decisions T1-625 and T1-628 with its addendum 1), starting within one day of the GA, with results by 2026-12-03: the full D4/D8 recall and question-answering rows (LongMemEval-S, 500 questions, and LoCoMo); Phase B's regression suites on each supported host build (the smoke stage ran Phase B's sweep and fault cells, above); and D5-B. The D4 mini row above ran before GA. A regression on a host build is handled as a hotfix, not left for the next release. Results are posted on [#3110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3110), and a regression in the area of [#3087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3087) found by these rows is posted there the same day it is read.
- D5, the clone run on a copy of the reference agent's store, had not run at GA. It runs after GA only on a stopped snapshot of that store taken through the plugin manager's ledger, in a window the plugin manager schedules, as a local copy that never leaves the test machine; otherwise it does not run. The tracking issue above records whether it ran.
- Not run: D1 LOCAL in full, for the same reason as its mini row above (owner decision, release decision T1-628 addendum 1). D1 OFF in full (above) showed 0 changed recall results (lcm_recall and full-text search) across 500 questions against v0.30.3.
- Not run: the D2/D3 facts-kept rows. Their comparison run cannot be judged until a reviewed spec change settles which summariser outcomes count as failures ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272), [#2273](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2273), [#2274](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2274)), as in v0.30.0 and v0.30.1. This release changes compaction, so it has no paired facts-kept evidence against v0.30.3; the D7 cell above is its facts-kept evidence. The release-readiness spec records these departures in its v0.30.4-only row, added by [#3109](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3109) before this tag.
